title: Cross-Energy of Dirichlet Partial Sums. Part 9: Zeros of the prime zeta function in its half-plane of absolute convergence
summary: The prime zeta function P(s) = ∑ₚ p⁻ˢ has zeros in its half-plane of absolute convergence. Belovas, Čepaitytė and Sabaliauskas proved that P(s) ≠ 0 for Re(s) > σₚ = 1.7795446535…, where σₚ solves P(σ) = 2¹⁻σ. We show that this bound is sharp: the closure of the real parts of the zeros in Re(s) > 1 is exactly [1, σₚ]. There are no zeros on Re(s) = σₚ, while zeros occur arbitrarily close to every line Re(s) = σ with 1 < σ < σₚ (Bohr’s method). By Jessen’s theorem, the density of real parts is J″(σ)/(2π), where J(σ) = −σ log 2 + 𝔼[log⁺(2^σ |Yσ|)], Yσ = ∑ₚ≥₃ p⁻σ eⁱθₚ, and the phases θₚ are…
